requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 on node1 via cron
requirements.summary: Executor created /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance with the line '15 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1', matching the requested schedule and target script. crond.service was confirmed active both immediately after creation and again after a full node restart, and the cron file was confirmed to persist post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Retain the maintenance script's output in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
requirements.summary: The log file was created/touched, and a manual invocation of the script showed its stdout being appended into /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log via the cron line's redirection syntax. A second manual run after the node restart appended a further line, and cat of the log showed both prior and new entries accumulated (append, not overwrite) confirming durable log retention.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — a daily 02:15 cron job running /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance and durable retention of its output in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log — are directly and coherently satisfied. The executor's /etc/cron.d entry matches the requested schedule and script exactly, and the log-append behavior was proven both before and after a full node restart, with the cron configuration, script, and prior log content all confirmed to survive the reboot alongside a fresh manual run appending correctly. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly for node1: a pre-restart baseline (boot id fe422859...), a restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot id (def448b5...), and full recovery of cron/service/log state were all captured, consistent with the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity cross-check.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timeout) in all three lifecycle snapshots, so native package-manager consistency could not be verified before or after the executor's changes, though nothing in the executor's actions involved package management.

The task did not specify a log rotation or retention-duration requirement beyond 'retain output', so only append/persistence behavior was verified; no explicit test of behavior over multiple cron firings across days was possible within the evidence window.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace: cmd-8f509493125e45c6 (script/cron/log setup) and cmd-a07daec5659e40a2 (manual run + crond reload/restart to validate the new cron syntax) are both directly tied to satisfying the task outcome. cmd-370a654e2b364ce5, cmd-fc9b06a2beef4cc7, and cmd-e6c950eb26b34d1c are read-only verification/diagnostic commands. cmd-54058190291141b2 (issuing a reboot) and the two failed polling attempts (cmd-8d8c4e3143a34811, cmd-995d97cfe2c442fe, expected non-zero exits during the outage window) are part of the separate provider-wide restart-evidence protocol rather than the public task contract, but this bounded, single-node reboot is a reasonable, low-risk mutation with clear evidence of full recovery (crond active, cron file, script, and log data all persisted) — no residue, no destructive or unbounded change. No unnecessary or abandoned mutations were found; lifecycle snapshot diffs show only expected reboot-related churn (boot id, ephemeral systemd-private tmp dirs, transient socket PIDs), not executor-caused residue.
